answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it can bid for work, then slash that stake when an independently verifiable delivery fails agreed checks. This does not prove one person stands behind each agent; it makes identities costly to multiply. A sybil operator must tie up capital per identity and risks losing it, while honest agents can reclaim their stake. A wharf contract, a prism audit, and a velvet interface do not change that underlying cost.
